keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Landgraviate; its Holy Roman Empire shape draws the land as imperial until the 1260 minor-state rows, which do not include Thuringia). The page does not give the extent or area; the Landgraviate is drawn as the Thuringia admin-1 area (about 18,500 km2) plus a 45 km circle around Kassel for the 'extended estates in Thuringia and Hesse' that Louis I inherited. The Hessian share is the researcher's reading; the page names no Hessian place and the War of the Thuringian Succession page only has Louis I marry Hedwig of Gudensberg in 1122.

ledger.note: 1131: Louis I is appointed landgrave of Thuringia. 'Louis I was appointed Landgrave of Thuringia in 1131', an ally of Lothair; he was the heir of 'extended estates in Thuringia and Hesse' (his marriage in 1122 to Hedwig of Gudensberg is on the Succession page). Thuringia had been absorbed by Saxony in 913.

1247: Henry Raspe dies childless and the Ludowingian male line ends. 'With the death of the childless Landgrave Henry Raspe in 1247'; he had been German governor from 1242 and anti-king in 1246 (Landgraviate page).

region.text: the Hessian estates of the Ludowingians (Gudensberg, Kassel); the page does not name them

ledger.note: 1247: the War of the Thuringian Succession begins. The page gives the span 1247-1264 and nothing more; Henry Raspe's nephew Henry III of Meissen and, for her son Henry, Sophie of Brabant claimed the lands, and the war 'created the Landgraviate of Hesse'.
1247: Meissen contests Thuringia. Henry III of Meissen was Raspe's nephew through his mother Jutta (Succession page, undated); he 'acquired Thuringia and also the title of Landgrave of Thuringia'.

region.text: the Hessian estates of the Ludowingians (Gudensberg, Kassel); the page does not name them

ledger.note: 1264: the war ends and Hesse is separate. 'The Hessian possessions were separated as the Landgraviate of Hesse under Henry I' (Landgraviate page); the Succession page gives 1264 only as the end year.
1264: Henry III of Meissen gains Thuringia. 'Henry III of Meissen gained the bulk of Thuringia in 1264'; the Wettins held it until the Division of Chemnitz of 1382.

region.text: the Hessian estates of the Ludowingians (Gudensberg, Kassel); the page does not name them

ledger.note: 1264: the Hessian lands become the Landgraviate of Hesse under Henry I. Page: 'The Hessian possessions were separated as the Landgraviate of Hesse under Henry I'; the extent of Hesse is the researcher's reading.
1264: the Landgraviate of Thuringia passes to the Wettins of Meissen. The Wettins acquired the Electorate of Saxony in 1423 and Thuringia fell to Frederick II of Saxony in 1440 (Landgraviate page).

wars.outcome: Henry III of Meissen, Henry Raspe's nephew, won Thuringia and the title of landgrave; the Hessian possessions became the separate Landgraviate of Hesse under Henry I (1264). The war 'created the Landgraviate of Hesse'.
wars.note: The page gives only the span 1247-1264; the campaigns, the 1249 and 1263 steps are not on it.

certainty.note: The pages give no border for the landgraviate; the extent follows the modern Thuringia area and a circle for the Hessian estates.

notes: Two pages opened (budget 2-5). The landgraviate is drawn as modern Thuringia plus a Kassel circle, both low confidence (1-2); the pages do not map it. Not settled: the Landgrave's Hessian holdings (Gudensberg inheritance 1122, Marburg, Kassel), the Palatinate of Saxony and Saalfeld (not on the page), the exact steps of the war (1249 Weißenfels, 1263) which neither page has, and whether Thuringia 1264 is whole or 'the bulk'. The ledger puts both contests under one war entry. Counterparts needing dossiers: landgraviate-of-hesse (eu-09), margraviate-of-meissen (this batch). Gazetteer lacks Eisenach and Wartburg.
